Latin word

dictum

dictum, dictī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a remark, something said; what someone has said, a statement

In this lexicon

  • comment

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.32.1: omnia omnium dicta … in mē cōnferrī; Traupman 353: dictum incūriōsum, offhand remark

  • statement

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 1.23: dictōrum conventōrumque cōnstantia et vēritās

  • dictum ac factum (dictum factum): no sooner said than done

    classical

  • Nūllum est jam dictum quod nōn dictum sit prius.: there is nothing new under the sun

    classical

  • Nīl dictum quod nōn prius dictum.: there is nothing new under the sun

    modern

Examples

  • ais enim, ut ego discesserim, omnia omnium dicta … in mē cōnferrī

    for you say that since I left, every witty remark anyone makes is being put down to meCic. Fam. 7.32.1

    In the entry for comment

  • id ergō est prōnūntiātum, quod est vērum aut falsum

    a statement, then, is whatever is either true or falseCic. Tusc. 1.14

    In the entry for statement

  • est enim jūs jūrandum affirmātiō religiōsa

    for an oath is a statement made under religious sanctionCic. Off. 3.104
